pk.s: The primary conductor passes through the ring; secondary terminals S1 and S2

typ: Ratio, for example 400/5 A or 100/1 A
items.mark: The nameplate shows ratio, class, burden and the terminals P1, P2, S1, S2.
items.test: See the detailed lesson: de-energised winding and ratio checks only.
items.note: Never open the secondary of an energised CT.

pk.s: Primary and secondary windings; secondary fused

typ: Accuracy class and rated burden in VA
items.mark: The nameplate shows the ratio, class, burden and the terminals A, N and a, n.
items.test: See the detailed lesson: de-energised winding and fuse checks.
items.note: Never short-circuit the secondary of a VT.

pk.s: Unidirectional types have a cathode stripe

typ: Standoff voltage, breakdown voltage and peak pulse power (for example 600 W)
Clamps surges on power and signal lines
items.mark: The voltage is in the part number (for example SMBJ12A). The stripe marks the cathode on unidirectional types.
items.test: Diode-test mode: unidirectional types read like a diode; a short means it has failed.

typ: Hold current and trip current in the datasheet
Low resistance when cool; resistance rises sharply when it trips
items.mark: The hold current is often printed on the body.
items.test: Measure the cold resistance and compare it with the datasheet.

pk.s: Two power terminals and two sense terminals

typ: Resistance in milliohms, for example 0.010 Ω
Power from 1 W to many watts
items.mark: Value printed, for example R010 = 0.010 Ω.
items.test: Use a four-wire milliohm meter or measure the voltage drop at a known current.

pk.s: Pitches of 3.5, 5.0 and 5.08 mm are common

typ: Rated current, voltage and wire size in the datasheet
items.mark: Pin numbers and ratings are on the housing or datasheet.
items.test: Continuity from the clamp to the PCB pin, with the circuit de-energised.
